ImageDescription.value: The red light accessory for the Action Max video game console.  Released in 1987 by Worlds of Wonder, it was a console that worked in conjunction with a VCR to play light gun "games".  Games came on VHS tapes and were on-rails shooters that featured no real interactive elements.  The console merely kept track of how many hits were scored during the game, utilizing an external red light to alert players to successful hits.

ImageDescription.value: The Amstrad GX4000, a video game console released by Amstrad in 1990.  This Europe-exclusive console was a repackaging of Amstrad's line of CPC Plus computers, offering direct conversions of CPC Plus titles.  It was only on the market for a short while before being discontinued.
